summary: The University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship supports doctoral candidates, domestic and international, whose research fits the strategic aims of the university and the faculty. In 2026 it gives a tax-free stipend of NZD 35,468 a year for up to 42 months of full-time study, plus the Student Services Fee and compulsory tuition fees, and for international students the single-student health insurance charge. There is no separate application: you ask to be considered on your doctoral programme application, and awards are decided in four rounds a year. International students qualify only if they are eligible to pay the domestic PhD fee, which in practice means a PhD enrolment.
eligibility_notes:
Who can hold it: you must be either a domestic student or an international student who is eligible to pay domestic fees for the doctoral programme. International students are eligible to pay domestic fees for the PhD, but not for DMedSc, DClinPsy, DocFA, EdD or DHSc, so they cannot hold this scholarship for those named doctorates.

You must not already hold a doctorate, have previously been paid a University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship, or already be enrolled in a doctoral programme (exceptions exist for approved transfers from a master's, transfers from another doctoral programme without a University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship, and some bridging-programme cases).

Admission comes first: you can be granted the scholarship only if you are eligible (or conditionally eligible) for admission to the doctoral programme. The PhD entry requirement is a postgraduate honours or master's degree at a University of Auckland equivalent of B+ in a relevant field, with a significant research project (dissertation or thesis). For overseas qualifications a Grade Point Equivalent of 6.0 on the 0-9 scale is typical. You need a preliminary research proposal and a supervisor who is available; meeting the academic requirements does not guarantee entry.

Guaranteed awards: applicants who are Māori or Pacific, have a New Zealand university qualifying programme GPA of 7.0 or above, and are offered a doctoral place are guaranteed a scholarship.

English: all doctoral candidates must meet the postgraduate English language requirement, equivalent to IELTS Academic 6.5 with no band below 6.0 (also TOEFL iBT 90 with writing 21, PTE Academic 58 with no Communicative score below 50, and other listed tests). Results are valid for two years and must be met in a single sitting; citizens of Canada, Ireland, Singapore, the UK and the USA are usually exempt. All candidates also complete the Diagnostic English Language Needs Assessment. Applicants who meet academic but not English requirements may get a conditional offer.

While holding the award: you must stay eligible for the domestic PhD fee, which for international students means living in New Zealand for the whole programme, with research or conference time overseas limited to a total of 12 months. You must not do more than 750 hours of additional paid work in any 12-month period. You must not hold it together with another University-funded doctoral scholarship or with a postgraduate award from Universities New Zealand or a foreign government or agency.
age_experience_notes: No age limit or work experience requirement is stated. Research experience is expected for entry: a completed research project such as a thesis or dissertation.
funding_summary: In 2026: a tax-free stipend of NZD 35,468 a year (pro-rated in the first year; adjusted each 1 January for CPI, with a 2.6% rise applied from 1 January 2026) for up to 42 months of full-time-equivalent doctoral enrolment, plus the Student Services Fee and compulsory tuition fees, and for international students the single-student health insurance compulsory charge. For an EdD or DHSc the stipend runs for up to 24 months of the thesis component. The award ends earlier if you first submit your thesis for examination, withdraw or your candidature is terminated. A separate six-month Doctoral Scholarship Extension exists for people who hold other funding.
programmes_note: The scholarship is for the PhD (and, for domestic students, the named doctorates DMedSc, DClinPsy, DocFA, EdD and DHSc). The University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship is awarded across all faculties and research centres, based on alignment with the university's and the faculty's strategic aims and each unit's published selection criteria. Faculties and institutes also advertise their own doctoral scholarships, with their own stipends: for example the Business School Dean's Doctoral Scholarship, Faculty of Engineering Doctoral Scholarship, Dean's International Doctoral Scholarship (Medical and Health Sciences), Law School Dean's Doctoral Scholarship and the Alan Maxwell Science PhD Scholarship.
institutions_note: University of Auckland only (Waipapa Taumata Rau). Selection is run by an advisory committee in each faculty, large-scale research institute or university research centre, which nominates applicants to the Pro Vice-Chancellor Global and Graduate Research; the Vice-Chancellor grants the award. The units are Arts and Education, Auckland Bioengineering Institute, Business and Economics, Engineering and Design, Law, Liggins Institute, Medical and Health Sciences, Science, and several research centres.

summary.detail: PhD at the University of Auckland for up to 42 months full-time equivalent. International students are eligible only for the PhD (domestic fee route). Part-time enrolment is only for New Zealand students. You must submit a Statement of Research Intent and find a supervisor; entry normally needs a master's or honours degree at B+ equivalent.

programmes.name: PhD (Doctor of Philosophy)
programmes.detail: Up to 42 months full-time equivalent; open to international students through the domestic PhD fee route

benefits.limit_text: Tax-free stipend of NZD 35,468 per year in 2026, for up to 42 months full-time equivalent
benefits.conditions: Pro-rated in the first year depending on start date; adjusted each 1 January by CPI (2.6% increase from 1 January 2026) and could fall if CPI is negative. Paid pro rata for part-time study. The scholarship is suspended while enrolment is suspended, and the stipend is not paid for a paid internship period where the internship income is at least the stipend. If you hold a second award, the total stipends must not exceed 150% of this stipend. For an EdD or DHSc, up to 24 months of the thesis part.

benefits.limit_text: Student Services Fee and compulsory tuition fees for the prescribed doctoral study
benefits.conditions: For up to 42 months full-time equivalent. International students receive this only if eligible for the domestic PhD fee (the 2027 international PhD tuition fee shown by the university is NZD 9,378 per year, at the domestic rate). If you lose domestic-fee eligibility you pay international fees.

benefits.limit_text: Single-student health insurance compulsory charge, for international students only
benefits.conditions: As shown on the tuition fee invoice. International students must have health and travel insurance.

benefits.limit_text: Accommodation is not listed as a component
benefits.conditions: The stipend may be used for living expenses; the terms say funds must be used for costs directly related to study, including living expenses.

benefits.limit_text: Travel and airfare are not listed as components
benefits.conditions: A separate doctoral research and travel scholarships page exists; it was not read.

benefits.limit_text: Doctoral Scholarship Extension: stipend at the same rate (NZD 17,734 in 2026), fees and health insurance charge for up to six months FTE
benefits.conditions: Only for people holding external funding worth at least 75% of the University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship for 36 months; foreign government or agency funding does not qualify. Apply at least three months before current funding ends.

requirements.text: Academic transcript for your highest tertiary qualification and any other relevant qualification, including the institution's grading scale.
English language test results (for example IELTS Academic 6.5 with no band below 6.0), valid for two years from the certificate date to the start of study.
requirements.conditional_rule: If English is not your first language and you are not exempt (citizens of Canada, Ireland, Singapore, the UK and the USA are usually exempt).

requirements.text: Statement of Research Intent: a one-page abstract-style statement on the University template, saved as a Word document. You also give a descriptive research topic and a proposed thesis title, each normally no more than 150 characters.
CV listing all complete and incomplete study, and publications if applicable.
Two confidential referee reports, arranged by you and confirmed in the application.
requirements.conditional_rule: If you have not studied at the University of Auckland in the past five years.

requirements.text: A statement in the application that you wish to be considered for the scholarship; no separate scholarship application is needed. You can also say if you already have scholarship funding.
Diagnostic English Language Needs Assessment (DELNA), completed by all doctoral candidates.

application_steps.title: Find a supervisor and check entry requirements
application_steps.detail: Find a supervisor through the university's supervisor search, research pages or a postgraduate adviser. PhD entry normally needs a master's or honours degree at B+ equivalent with a research project; overseas qualifications are typically assessed at a Grade Point Equivalent of 6.0. Nominating a supervisor on the form is optional.

application_steps.title: Apply for the doctoral programme and ask to be considered
application_steps.detail: Complete the online Application for Admission: personal summary, academic history, programme choice, start month, research topic, thesis title, supporting documents. Say you wish to be considered for the scholarship; there is no separate scholarship application. Your start date should be no more than nine months after you submit. The four 2027 rounds close on 1 November 2026, 1 February 2027, 1 May 2027 and 1 August 2027, according to when your programme application is submitted.

application_steps.title: Faculty committee ranks and nominates applicants
application_steps.detail: Each faculty, institute or research centre advisory committee considers the applications in each round and nominates applicants, based on alignment with the university's and the faculty's strategic aims and the unit's published criteria, within its yearly allocation. A committee may nominate no one in a round if no application is aligned enough. Equity, diversity and inclusion aims are also considered. The Vice-Chancellor grants the award after the recommendation. You must be eligible, or conditionally eligible, for admission.

application_steps.title: Outcome by the offer date for your round
application_steps.detail: Scholarship offers are made by 1 February 2027, 1 April 2027, 1 July 2027 or 1 October 2027 for the four rounds respectively. The university may decide an application in a later round if it cannot finish in time. Do not enrol until the scholarship has been considered and you have been told the outcome. If your qualifying programme is unfinished, you may get a conditional scholarship offer or conditional admission.

application_steps.title: Take up the award and enrol on time
application_steps.detail: The scholarship must be taken up by the date in the letter of award or it is forfeited. You need unconditional enrolment within four calendar months of the award if your qualifying programme is from New Zealand, or within seven months if it is from overseas. International students may need a funding letter for the visa, which can be requested through Student Services Online. International PhD students can enrol from the dates shown for their round.

application_steps.title: Keep to the scholarship conditions
application_steps.detail: Tell the Scholarships Office about changes to enrolment or funding, including suspension or another award. Do not exceed 750 hours of additional paid work per 12 months. Suspension of up to 12 months in total is allowed (a further 12 months for becoming a parent or compelling reasons, with approval); longer ends the scholarship. The scholarship ends when you first submit your thesis, withdraw, or your candidature ends. After a PhD, graduates can apply for a three-year post-study work visa, and a partner can get an open work permit for the length of the PhD, according to the university's international student page.

Stored dates were not given; the 2027 rounds (apply by 1 November 2026, 1 February, 1 May and 1 August 2027) were read on the official scholarship page.

The international students page says PhD students have unlimited work rights under the student visa, but the scholarship terms cap additional paid work at 750 hours per 12 months while holding the award: the scholarship rule is the one that applies to award holders.
Faculty doctoral scholarships on the international scholarships page show older stipend figures (some labelled 2024) and 36-month durations; check each faculty page before relying on those.
